artifactType: Backlog 2 Batch 026 staged manual extraction input
scope: Fixed membership S3942, S4732, S4562, S3935, S5004 only
modelNote: The skill-default GPT-5.5 runner was not selectable in this delegated workspace; this staged pass uses the available local GPT-5 Codex model.

checks: All five live primary attachments were downloaded once from the attached paper_files record and SHA-256 matched papers.primary_file_sha256 before source inspection.

Population layouts were selected before field staging: Total / 1st Bundesliga / 2nd Bundesliga (S3942); Total / Match / Training (S4562 and S3935); Football 5-a-side (S5004); none for the S4732 systematic-review exclusion.

Tabs 1-4 were staged for each eligible primary study. Every results table and usable figure was swept once for Tabs 5-10; fields are confined to directly reported values or explicitly documented compatible sums of direct subrows.
S4732 explicitly identifies itself as a systematic review and meta-analysis of five RCTs, so no primary-cohort extraction is staged.

S5004 is a multisport paper, but Tables 2 and 5 give a clean direct football-5-a-side subgroup. Only that football subgroup is staged; all-sport Tables 1, 3, 4 and 6 are not forced into football fields.
No exposure, count, burden, or time-loss total was back-calculated from a rate. The only arithmetic used is transparent summation of directly printed compatible subgroup rows, marked in caveats.

sourceCoverage.S3942: Primary PDF pp. 1-8: abstract, methods/definitions, Tables I-VII, Figures 1-3, results, illness paragraph, discussion and limitations checked. Supplementary tables were not attached to the live primary PDF.

sourceCoverage.S4562: Primary PDF pp. 1-24: abstract, methods/definitions, Table 1, Tables 2-4, Figure 1, results, discussion, limitations and conclusion checked. Supplementary medical-attention tables are referenced but not attached to the live primary PDF.
sourceCoverage.S3935: Primary PDF pp. 1-7: abstract, methods/definitions, Tables 1-3, Figures 1-2, results, discussion, limitations and conclusion checked.
sourceCoverage.S5004: Primary PDF pp. 1-9: abstract, methods/definitions, Tables 1-6, results, discussion and conclusion checked. Football-specific Table 2 injury and Table 5 illness rows are staged; Tables 1, 3, 4 and 6 are all-sport only.

studyDetails.title: Injury epidemiology in male professional German football: a long-term comparison between the two highest national leagues
studyDetails.journal: The Journal of Sports Medicine and Physical Fitness

participantCharacteristics.levelOfPlay: elite male professional first-team football; 1st and 2nd Bundesliga

definitions.injuryDefinition: medical attention [physical complaint from football exposure, irrespective of absence]
definitions.incidenceDefinition: injuries per 1000 player-hours of match or training exposure
definitions.burdenDefinition: days lost per 1000 player-hours of match or training exposure
definitions.severityDefinition: mild 0-3 days; minor 4-7 days; moderate 8-28 days; severe >28 days
definitions.recurrenceDefinition: same body part and structure within 1 year of the immediately preceding injury

caveats: The primary result axis is league level, so the payload is Total / 1st Bundesliga / 2nd Bundesliga. Global participant and illness values remain only on the Total line.

Training exposure values are transparent sums of the directly printed season-specific Table IV minutes, converted to hours: 68,866.5 total / 34,724.4 first division / 34,142.2 second division. The narrative's isolated 17,217-hour wording is not used because it conflicts with its own complete Table IV season totals.

Table V incidence and Table VI burden are Poisson estimates and therefore are retained directly rather than recalculated from injury counts/exposure. The schema has no match/training-specific CI or burden fields, so their directly printed orientations are named inline.

The only directly countable main-PDF tissue row is tendon injury (59 versus 38). Detailed body-region injury counts are referenced only in absent supplementary tables, so no location family is forced from prose or figures.
The source reports illness totals only across the eight-season cohort; illness subgroup rows are intentionally blank.

caveats: Results states 114 participating players; the abstract's 95-player figure describes the group with medical-attention injuries, so the direct 114 participant total is used.

The Total player-hour exposure (7247.6) is the transparent sum of directly reported match (326.6) and training (6921) exposure; the separate illness denominator is 5611 player-days and is not conflated with player-hours.

The source directly reports all-injury and time-loss metrics separately. Direct CIs are retained by matching Total / Match / Training row; the generic schema CI field therefore names both metrics rather than silently attaching them to only one rate.

Tables 2-4 provide time-loss-only structured rows. Total structured counts are sums of direct Match and Training counts; rates, burden, and median time loss remain on their source-specific Match/Training lines because their denominators differ. Median values are labelled in mean-days fields because the schema has no structured median field.

Contact is the transparent sum of directly reported opponent-direct and opponent-indirect contact; no count is inferred for ground, ball, or other mechanisms. The 17 reinjuries are medical-attention events and are not treated as a time-loss-only rate.
Supplementary medical-attention structured tables were not attached, so no all-medical-attention tissue/location family is inferred.

studyDetails.title: One competitive season of injuries in professional football: a retrospective study from a Portuguese first league team

definitions.injuryDefinition: time loss [physical complaint from football activity causing at least one missed official match]
definitions.severityDefinition: mild 1-3 weeks; moderate 3-6 weeks; severe >6 weeks
definitions.recurrenceDefinition: same type and location within 6 weeks of return to full participation

caveats: The source directly reports Total / Match / Training injury counts and rates, but not player-hour totals; it supplies a usable direct rate denominator, so the paper remains extractable and no exposure is back-calculated.
The two unclassifiable insidious-onset injuries are explicitly incorporated by the paper into the Training incidence group, making the direct training count 18.

Table 2's Hip/Thigh block is mapped only through direct individual rows: thigh=10 (semitendinosus, biceps femoris, hamstring tendon, rectus femoris, vastus) and groin=4 (adductor longus). Knee=6 and lower leg=1 similarly preserve the direct Table 2 diagnoses; lower limb=25 is the compatible direct sum of all lower-limb subrows.
Shoulder dislocation has no direct schema row and is represented only as the upper-limb/shoulder location count; no unsupported dislocation tissue mapping is forced.
The mean 20.8 is the paper's average training days missed per injury; median 15 and severity categories are total-cohort values only.

studyDetails.title: Incidence of injury and illness at the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games: post-pandemic trends and sport-specific risks

definitions.injuryDefinition: medical attention [IOC and Para sport consensus definitions]
definitions.illnessDefinition: medical attention [IOC and Para sport consensus definitions]
definitions.mechanismReporting: team medical staff via WEB-IISS and local organising medical services

caveats: This is a multisport surveillance study. The staged record is restricted to the directly reported Football 5-a-side row (64 athletes, 896 athlete-days); no all-sport participant, sex, age, location, injury-type, illness-system, time-loss-count, or mechanism figure is copied into the football subgroup.

Table 2 directly reports 19 football-5-a-side injuries, incidence 22.3 (14.4-37.7), and discussion directly reports its burden 23.4 (6.2-88.3). Table 5 directly reports 7 illnesses and incidence 10.0 (4.5-22.4).
Tables 1, 3, 4 and 6 do not split structural injury/illness families by football, so Tabs 7-10 are intentionally blank rather than using all-sport rows.
